prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: porting a mortgage to a new property. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member wants to port a mortgage, check early whether the existing deal actually allows porting and whether the new property is acceptable security, because the decision often turns on both points."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the porting request is linked to a house move, I need to treat the existing loan and the new borrowing as separate checks, even if they are part of one overall plan."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the new property is more expensive than the old one, I should expect the member to need extra borrowing and re-run affordability on the full amount rather than assuming the old payment pattern will still fit."},{"type":"preference","content":"When timing is tight, I prefer to confirm the sale and purchase dates, the expiry of the current product, and any early repayment charge window straight away, so we do not miss a porting deadline."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member is moving to a smaller loan, I should check whether any overpayment or partial repayment would trigger charges or reduce the amount that can be ported, because the details matter."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a porting case involves a change in term, rate, or borrowing level, I should document the exact structure carefully, as the new arrangement may not mirror the old mortgage even though the deal is being ported."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the property type changes, such as from standard house to flat or leasehold, I need to review title, tenure, and any building-specific restrictions, since those can affect acceptability even for an existing borrower."},{"type":"preference","content":"When evidence is incomplete, I prefer to ask for the missing income, expenditure, and property documents before giving any expectation of success, because assumptions create avoidable delays."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the customer is porting after a relationship change or a joint-to-single application, I must reassess who will remain liable and whether the remaining applicant can support the new borrowing on their own."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the old mortgage is portable but the new case needs a fresh underwriting decision, I should explain clearly that porting is not automatic approval, as the new property and affordability can still lead to decline."}]}
